transcriptSegments.text: Hello, can I help you?
Hi, I'm still a student but I've done a bit of research into the tea company you work for
and I have a few questions about the tea tasters jobs you have advertised.
Well, that's actually what I do.
Would you like me to tell you a bit about what it's like being a trainee tea taster? Yes, please.
Well, initially, even though there's some time spent in meetings at our office, a
trainee is based in our lab for most of their time being trained how to do the tasting. Right.
How do you actually learn how to taste tea?
Do you use a special kind of cup?
No, rather than that or even a glass to do the tasting, we sip it from a spoon. Ah, OK.
And what other kind of things will I need to learn?
Well, there are many different qualities of tea, so one of the most important things is to learn how to decide which grade should be assigned to each sample.
That's a very important part of the job.
Yes, I can see why.
And then another important thing to learn is how to choose the right leaf for tea bags.
Shape isn't nearly as important as the size in that case.
Gosh, I'd never really thought about what goes into a tea bag.
So do all of the teas have their own name?
Yes, that's another important part of the training.
It took me ages before I remembered them all. I can imagine.
So how long before I qualify?
I heard it was seven years, is that right?
Well, it used to be, but we've speeded things up a bit, so now it only takes five.
That's two years less than before, which is quite significant, really. Right, I see.
The job sounds really interesting, but what I'd like to know before applying is what kind of person you're looking for.
That way I can see whether I'll be a good fit.
Well, you need to have a degree. Well, that's fine. I'm just finishing mine.
However, it doesn't have to be a science degree, even though that's a definite bonus.
My degree was in history, for example. I'm studying languages. Yes, that'll be fine. Is there anything else?
Yes, you need to be able to do maths and do it fast.
A lot of the job is to do with the price of tea, so that's really important.
OK, that makes sense.
And this might seem unusual, but you'll have your sight tested.
We're not worried about whether you need glasses or not, that's fine, but you have to see colour accurately.
It's very important when looking at tea leaves.
Wow, I'd never have thought about that, but it makes sense.
What about other things, like how important is good communication? Essential.
You'll need to be highly skilled at that, as you'll meet such varied people in this job, everyone from farmers to buyers.
OK, I've noted that. Anything else I should remember?
Yes, I'd say there's no point doing this job if you don't like to travel.
You'll be living out of a suitcase for a while, so if you're not worried about spending time abroad, for example, that'll work in your favour.
OK, well, thanks for all the information.
You've been so helpful.
Hello, everyone, and welcome to Pioneer Historical Village.
It's an outdoor park recreated to look just like a village from the mid-19th century.
Visitors can wander through the village, look inside the houses, and get a feel for what life was like back then.
The village has grown somewhat since it was first opened to the public, going back a bit,
in 1962 a committee was formed in the hope of preserving some of the local history.
Many years of planning and fundraising followed.
Volunteers worked throughout the 1970s to restore and move buildings to the site.
In 1980 the village welcomed its first paying visitors.
We'll go in now, and I'll help you purchase your tickets.
Since there are 10 of you all together in this party, you qualify for the group discount.
The normal price of admission is $16 for adults and $12.50 for students and seniors,
but it'll only be $11 per person for all of you today, which is quite a saving.
Sometimes we have shows and demonstrations.
